title: Repo-wide temp-dir leak: moe-release-* fixture dirs accumulate under $env:TEMP across suites
description:
Filed by governor-e01ddc57 on 2026-08-19 from worker-21246c33's disclosure in REVIEW of task-59c16705 (msg-19ad38f3) — measured, not inferred, and explicitly NOT widened into that one-file task.

MEASURED at 2026-08-19 ~21:54Z: $env:TEMP holds 15,401 `moe-release-*` directories dating back to 2026-08-17. Only 9 belong to release-archive-cleanup.test.ts (fixed for new leaks at a796b87). The bulk are OTHER suites: moe-release-slot 3,343 · moe-release-draining 1,998 · moe-release-omitted 1,202 · moe-release-released 804 · moe-release-counter 777 · remainder across further prefixes.

DEFECT CLASS (same as task-59c16705's clause 2): fixture teardowns that rmSync without maxRetries/retryDelay and/or prune their pending-roots list before removal succeeds, so the first EPERM (child still holding the dir, AV touch, spawn-cliff timeout) silently leaks every remaining dir. Any host event that interrupts a suite mid-fixture (e.g. the 2026-08-19 mtkbtsvc spawn cliff) mass-produces them.

FIX SHAPE (planner's call): inventory every fixture family creating moe-release-* dirs (grep mkdtemp over the test tree); extract/reuse the hardened teardown pattern from tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts at a796b87 (`removeTemporaryRoots`: iterate a copy, retry with maxRetries/retryDelay, prune ONLY after successful removal, index-guarded splice, collect-then-throw RELEASE_ARCHIVE_TEARDOWN_LEAK-style report) into a shared helper rather than N copies; per-suite adoption. Pre-existing dirs on any given host are evidence/hygiene, not a test assertion target — assert ZERO NEW dirs per run (delta), never absolute-zero on a dirty host (task-59c16705 review established delta grading).

Prior art / cautions: mutation drills per epic rail 6 (prune-before-remove and retry-removal mutants must red — see 59c16705 steps 4/6 for the drill shapes and the known drill-(b)-throws-at-call-site limitation); a leak-repair test must not itself leak on its failing path (finally-wrap, defect found and fixed in 59c16705's own review).
definitionOfDone: An inventory (in the plan or a step note) names every fixture family that creates moe-release-* temp dirs and which file owns each
A shared teardown helper (or documented per-suite equivalent) applies retry + prune-after-success + collect-then-report semantics to every inventoried family
A full-suite run leaves ZERO NEW moe-release-* dirs under $env:TEMP (delta assertion, before/after counts cited); pre-existing dirs are not swept by tests
Mutation drills prove the helper live at least once per mechanism (prune-before-remove mutant reds; retry-removal mutant reds), byte-exact restores verified

implementationPlan.description: CONFIRM THE INVENTORY (DoD 1 — measured at plan time at HEAD, re-verify at yours). Every moe-release-* creator in the repo, by grep `moe-release-` over *.ts/*.mjs: (1) tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts:34,:170 (moe-release-archive-, moe-release-teardown-) — ALREADY HARDENED at a796b87 (removeTemporaryRoots: iterate copy, outer retry, prune-after-success, collect-then-throw RELEASE_ARCHIVE_TEARDOWN_LEAK) — the reference pattern, NO EDIT. (2) apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.test.ts:138 activated(label) and :637 plantedSlot(label) — THE 15K BULK (labels slot-*, draining-then-settled, omitted-*, released*, counter-* map exactly to the governor's measured prefixes): both mkdtempSync roots are NEVER REGISTERED anywhere — the file's afterEach(cleanupRestoreHarnesses) (:52) removes only roots the harness tracks, and openHarnessStore registers only STORES — so these dirs leak UNCONDITIONALLY on every run, not merely on EPERM. (3) apps/daemon/src/recovery/restore-test-harness.ts:69 cleanupRestoreHarnesses — shared by ~10 daemon suites; its rmSync has maxRetries:5 but the loop is `roots.pop()` BEFORE rmSync: a post-retry throw loses the popped root AND aborts the while loop, leaking the remainder — the same prune-before-success class. (4) tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs:20 (moe-release-test-), teardown :26 `while (temporary.length > 0) rmSync(temporary.pop(), …)` — pop-before-remove, no retry, throw aborts loop. (5) scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs:264 (moe-release-build-), cleanup :241-242 — splice(0) up front but per-root try/catch (continues; leaks only the failing root, reported via console.error) and NO maxRetries; also the :146 temporary rmSync. Record this inventory in the step note verbatim with your re-measured line numbers, plus the CURRENT $env:TEMP count: `(Get-ChildItem $env:TEMP -Filter 'moe-release-*' -Directory).Count` from PowerShell (was 15,401 at 2026-08-19 21:54Z).
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 1 DONE — inventory re-measured at my HEAD. **Every clause of the plan's inventory holds**, and the count has grown since the filing.

**CURRENT CENSUS, PowerShell, 2026-08-19 ~23:05Z: 17,073 `moe-release-*` dirs** — up from the governor's 15,401 at 21:54Z, i.e. **+1,672 in about 70 minutes**. That rate is explained: I ran `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` roughly a dozen times during the last two tasks, and the disposition suite leaks unconditionally on every run. Prefix distribution matches the filing almost exactly: `slot` 3,875 · `draining` 2,188 · `omitted` 1,316 · `released` 880 · `counter` 853 · `divergent` 553.

**THE FIVE CREATORS (`git grep -n "moe-release-" -- '*.ts' '*.mjs'`), with my line numbers:**
1. `apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.test.ts:138` (`activated`) and `:637` (`plantedSlot`) — **THE BULK, and it is NOT an EPERM story.** Both do `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), \`moe-release-${label}-\`))` and **never register the root anywhere**. Confirmed by reading both functions: they pass the path straight into `openHarnessStore`, and `openHarnessStore` (restore-test-harness.ts:83-88) pushes only STORES. So `afterEach(cleanupRestoreHarnesses)` closes the handles and removes nothing. **These leak on the green path, every run, with no host event required** — which is why the count grows monotonically with test runs rather than with incidents.
2. `apps/daemon/src/recovery/restore-test-harness.ts:69-80` — `cleanupRestoreHarnesses`. `roots` IS a live array (pushed at `:162` and `:305`, so the loop is not dead code), and its `rmSync` already carries `maxRetries: 5`. The defect is the loop shape: `const root = roots.pop()` happens BEFORE `rmSync`, so a post-retry throw **loses the popped root AND aborts the `while`**, leaking every root behind it. Shared by ~10 daemon suites.
3. `tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs:26` — `while (temporary.length > 0) rmSync(temporary.pop(), { force: true, recursive: true })`: pop-before-remove, **no retry options at all**, and a throw aborts the loop.
4. `scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs:264` creates `moe-release-build-`; cleanup at `:241-242` splices up front but wraps each removal in its own try/catch (continues, reports via `console.error`) — so it leaks only the failing root. Missing only the retry options.
5. `tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts:34` / `:170` — **the FIXED reference** (`removeTemporaryRoots`, a796b87). No edit; it is the pattern the rest adopt.

**THREE DISTINCT DEFECT SHAPES**, which is why one fix does not cover all four sites: (i) **never registered** (the 15k bulk — a registration fix, not a retry fix); (ii) **prune-before-success + abort-on-throw** (harness, .mjs); (iii) **no retry options** (.mjs, production script). The plan's per-site treatment matches each shape, and I will not paper over (i) with a retry it never needed.

**Nothing edited in this step.** Next: step 2's RED against `trackHarnessRoot` and the hardened cleanup.

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED — the shared harness gets the hardened semantics and a way to track fixture roots. Cases against not-yet-existing exports: (a) `trackHarnessRoot(root: string): string` registers an mkdtemp dir so cleanupRestoreHarnesses removes it — create two REAL temp dirs, track both, run cleanup, assert existsSync false for both and the pending list empty; (b) TRANSIENT failure (DoD 4 mechanism 1): with an injectable remover (or a first-call-throws EPERM wrapper delegating to real rmSync — mirror the a796b87 test shape at tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts), one throw-then-succeed leaves ZERO dirs and an emptied list — reds if the outer retry is removed; (c) PERSISTENT failure (DoD 4 mechanism 2): remover that always throws for dir A, delegates for B — cleanup removes B, KEEPS exactly A in the pending list (prune-after-success — this assertion is the prune-before-remove mutant killer), and REPORTS the leak with a stable prefix (RESTORE_HARNESS_TEARDOWN_LEAK: <dir>: <error> — collect-then-throw, matching the landed pattern; store-close semantics unchanged); try/finally real-rmSync A so the regression test itself leaks nothing; (d) stores still closed before roots are removed (current ordering preserved — a held SQLite handle on win32 is exactly the EPERM source). Run focused: RED (exports absent).
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 2 DONE — TDD RED. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/recovery/restore-test-harness.test.ts` **EXIT 1**, `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Tests 4 failed (4)` — all four fail on the absent exports `trackHarnessRoot` and `pendingHarnessRoots`, which is the red this step asks for. Unlike a missing MODULE, the file loads, so each case reds individually rather than collapsing into one suite-load error.

FOUR CASES, each pinning one mechanism:
- **(a) registration** — two REAL temp dirs tracked, cleanup runs, both gone and the pending list empty.
- **(b) transient** — an injected remover throws EPERM once for the first root then delegates to the real `rmSync`; asserts the refusal actually happened (`refused === true`, so the case cannot pass by never exercising the arm), both dirs gone, list empty. This is the retry-removal drill's target.
- **(c) persistent** — the remover always throws for one root and delegates for the other. Asserts the throw carries `RESTORE_HARNESS_TEARDOWN_LEAK` AND the failing path, that the root BEHIND the failure is still removed (a throw must not abort the sweep — the defect that loses the remainder), and that the pending list holds **exactly** the failing root. That last assertion is the prune-before-remove mutant killer.
- **(d) ordering** — stores close before roots are removed, preserved because a held SQLite handle is precisely the win32 EPERM source a retry cannot fix.

DISCIPLINE: every directory is real and removed on every exit path — case (c) wraps its assertions in `try/finally` with a real `rmSync` of the stuck root, and the file's `afterEach` drains any pending roots directly before calling cleanup inside a `try/catch`. A leak-repair test that leaks on its own failing path is the same defect wearing a different hat, and that exact bug was found in this pattern's first outing (task-59c16705's review).

DESIGN NOTE for step 3: `cleanupRestoreHarnesses` gains an OPTIONAL remover parameter defaulted to `rmSync`, so ~10 existing daemon callers keep their zero-argument call unchanged, and `pendingHarnessRoots()` exposes the list read-only so the prune-after-success property is assertable without exporting the array itself.

implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 DONE — GREEN, and **the 15k-per-run leak is measurably closed**. Owned suites: `restore-test-harness.test.ts` + `attempt-release-disposition.test.ts` + `runtime-entrypoint.test.ts` = **3 files / 44 tests, EXIT 0**. `pnpm run test:integration` EXIT 0 (11 files / 330 tests; node:test 66 pass / 0 fail).

**THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT.** Disposition suite alone, PowerShell, before/after the same run: **before=17,205 after=17,205, delta=0**, 35/35 passing. That suite was the bulk producer. For contrast, the run I took while it was still failing mid-adoption leaked **+44 in one run** — which at a dozen runs a session is exactly how five figures accumulated.

WHAT LANDED:
1. `restore-test-harness.ts` — `trackHarnessRoot(root)` (registers and returns, so a caller wraps its `mkdtempSync` in place), `pendingHarnessRoots()` (read-only, so prune-after-success is assertable), and the sweep rewritten to the a796b87 semantics: iterate a COPY, per-root 2-attempt retry around `rmSync({force, maxRetries: 5, recursive, retryDelay: 100})`, prune only after the removal SUCCEEDS, continue past failures, collect and throw ONE `RESTORE_HARNESS_TEARDOWN_LEAK: …`. Stores still close first — a held SQLite handle IS the win32 EPERM a retry cannot fix.
2. `attempt-release-disposition.test.ts` — `activated()` `:138` and `plantedSlot()` `:637` now wrap their `mkdtempSync` in `trackHarnessRoot(...)`. Two one-line changes; nothing else moved.
3. `tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs` — pop-loop replaced by the same three semantics inline, with a comment naming why it cannot import the TS helper (`node --test` `.mjs` cannot load a `.ts` module) and pointing at the reference implementation.
4. `scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs` — **options only**: `maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 100` added at the two `rmSync` sites. The `release temporary cleanup failed: …` message format and the splice/per-root-catch shape are untouched, because landed suites assert that string verbatim.

**TWO DEFECTS I CAUSED AND FIXED, both worth keeping as lessons:**

**(a) Giving a vitest HOOK function a parameter breaks every suite that passes it directly.** My first cut made `cleanupRestoreHarnesses(remove = rmSync)` injectable. ~10 suites do `afterEach(cleanupRestoreHarnesses)`, and **vitest reads a hook's ARITY**: a 1-parameter function is treated as the legacy `done`-callback style, so vitest passed its own `done` as my `remove`, and the first call died with `Error: done() callback is deprecated, use promise instead`. It reddened **31 of 35** disposition cases. Fixed by splitting: `cleanupRestoreHarnesses()` stays ZERO-arity for the hooks and delegates to an exported `sweepHarnessRoots(remove = rmSync)` where nothing is a hook. The reason is now a comment in the file so the next person does not re-add the parameter.

**(b) Adding a `.test.ts` sibling to a test-harness module PROMOTES it to runtime tier and demands `.js` bridges.** `runtime-entrypoint.test.ts` defines runtime tier as a forward closure seeded by the package entry **plus every module carrying its own `<name>.test.ts` sibling** — "a module under direct test is a published unit". Creating `restore-test-harness.test.ts` therefore pulled `restore-test-harness.ts` into the tier, and the closure dragged `bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts` with it (the harness imports it by `.js` specifier). The sweep reported `missing: ["recovery\\restore-test-harness.ts", "bootstrap\\bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts"]`. Added both one-line LF bridges in the exact form the sweep computes (`export * from "./<name>.ts";`); that suite is now 5/5.

**FOREIGN CHURN, disclosed, untouched.** Two files are being edited live by other sessions and flipped under me inside this step: `src/work/safe-boundary-observation.{ts,test.ts}` — **uncommitted peer edits to a task of mine now in REVIEW**; they went 12 passed -> 5 failed between two runs minutes apart, and the peer has already replaced my `derivedAt` fallback with `completedAt ?? startedAt ?? NO_DURABLE_INSTANT` (a real fix to a real defect of mine: the old `wall:<seconds>` string is not a canonical `decidedAt` and the store refuses it). And `src/work/foundation-context-manifest-reader.test.ts` (`FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_READER_NONCANONICAL` expected, `_UNREADABLE` received) — a third session. **I neither staged, edited nor stashed any of them**, and none is an owned path of this task.

implementationPlan.note:
STEP 4 DONE — three drills, each alone, each restored with `git diff` proven **0 bytes** before the next. All three RED; none stayed green, so nothing needed strengthening.

**DRILL 1 — PRUNE-BEFORE-REMOVE.** Moved the `roots.indexOf` / `splice` pair ABOVE the `if (!removed)` guard in `sweepHarnessRoots`, so a root leaves the pending list whether or not it was actually removed:

  `AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]` — the pending list came back empty where it must hold exactly the stuck root. That assertion is the killer for the original defect shape.

**DRILL 2 — RETRY REMOVAL.** `attempt < 2` -> `attempt < 1`:
  × `retries a transient removal failure instead of abandoning the root`. One EPERM then success is no longer survivable, which is the mechanism the a796b87 pattern exists for.

**DRILL 3 — REGISTRATION, and it is the one that proves the BULK fix.** Reverted `trackHarnessRoot(...)` in `activated()` only, then ran a SINGLE case (`-t "releases the planted CONTROL"`, `Tests 1 passed | 34 skipped`) with a full before/after directory listing rather than a count:

**One case, one leaked directory, named.** That is the direct evidence that the registration edit — not the retry and not the prune order — is what stops the unconditional green-path leak, and it is why the other two drills alone would not have proved this task's main claim.

**Drill hygiene, per DoD 3's no-sweeping rule:** the leaked directory was deleted by **exact literal path** (`Remove-Item -LiteralPath`), verified gone, and the census returned to 17,241. **No wildcard sweep was run at any point** — a `moe-release-*` wildcard under `$env:TEMP` would have destroyed the 17k of pre-existing evidence this task is explicitly forbidden from touching.
